title: WPMS/495/2013 of M/S AGARWAL BROTHERS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 495 of 2013
M/s Agarwal Brothers Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. S.K. Posti, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Additional C.S.C., present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Honíble Kalyan Jyoti Sengupta, J. (Oral)
 In my view, in this matter alternative remedy is there
and the petitioner would be free to avail of such remedy, as
permissible under the law. Considering the urgency and having
regard to the fact that the petitionerís commercial goods are
detained, I think, for an interim measure for release of the goods
may be taken.
 In the event, the petitioner deposit 25 percent of the
demanded amount in cash, furnishes bank guarantee in any
Nationalised Bank for the 50 percent of the demanded amount and
furnishing a personal bond securing balance 25 percent of the
claim then the petitionerís goods shall be released within 48 hours
from the time of such deposit and furnishing. This deposit as well
as furnishing bank guarantee and personal bond will abide by the
result of the appeal, if preferred.
 If the petitioner succeeds in the appeal then amount so
to be deposited shall be refunded along with interest @ 9 percent
per annum and the bank guarantee shall also be returned and so
also personal surety. If no appeal is preferred by the petitioner
within a period of limitation, it would be open for the department to
appropriate the amount so to be deposited and encash the bank
guarantee and also enforce the surety bond. This disposes of the
writ petition.
 No order as to costs.
(K.J. Sengupta, J.)
13.03.2013
ASWAL
